subject.title: macOS launchd: plugin/config maintenance can leave Control UI in broken partial-reload state; restart may require doctor --fix

question: Should the remaining work define a shared partial-reload/readiness contract across Gateway readiness, `sessions.resolve`, restart recovery, and Control UI, or should maintainers intentionally limit this to the narrower WebChat recovery-notice path?
rationale: Source inspection shows several partial protections but no single product contract for the misleading live-but-not-ready state; choosing the boundary affects user-visible UX, gateway RPC semantics, and launchd recovery behavior.

options.title: Define Shared Degraded-State Contract
options.body: Make Gateway expose a temporary reload/not-ready state that session RPCs and Control UI can render consistently, then validate it on macOS launchd.

options.title: Accept Narrow WebChat Notice Scope
options.body: Land or reject the linked WebChat notice PR as the only near-term fix and leave broader restart/readiness semantics for a later explicitly sponsored design.

options.title: Require Fresh Live Repro First
options.body: Pause design work until a current-main macOS launchd replay proves which remaining symptom still occurs after crash-loop and readiness changes.

recommendation.title: Define Shared Degraded-State Contract
recommendation.body: Make Gateway expose a temporary reload/not-ready state that session RPCs and Control UI can render consistently, then validate it on macOS launchd.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice crosses gateway readiness, Control UI UX, session recovery, and product-scope boundaries where this history shows repeated adjacent ownership.
